paragraphs: July runs on your ruler. Mars spends the month in Gemini, your solar third house of errands, messages, and neighborhood logistics, and it opens loudly. Mars meets Uranus on July 4, which is the sky's version of a group chat catching fire. There may be a surprise text, a sudden plan, or a detour that turns out to matter. The quick ones can be fun to say yes to, though it helps to reread before you hit send.

The month's real weight sits at home. The Sun squares Saturn in your sign on July 6, and the friction is familiar: obligations to family or household pressing against what you are trying to become. The new moon in Cancer on July 14 offers a fresh start under your own roof, whether that is a lease, a conversation, or a room finally cleared. Mercury has been retrograde in the same territory all month. It stations direct on July 23, so domestic negotiations and paperwork may settle more easily after that date.

Two stations land in Aries itself. Neptune turns retrograde on July 7, and Saturn follows on July 26. Both are slow background weather rather than daily news, but the Saturn station is worth noticing. The discipline project you started this spring may come up for review through the end of the year. You might keep what held and let go of what was posture.

Then the sky turns lighter. The Sun enters Leo and your fifth house of pleasure, romance, and self-made things on July 22, and meets Jupiter there on July 29. That is a bright day this month for a launch, a date, or an opening night. The same day's full moon in Aquarius lights your house of friends and future plans, so something you make for joy may find its audience. Mars sextile Saturn on July 19 already showed that speed and structure can, for once, sit on the same side.

Money moves first this month. Mars and Uranus share Gemini, your solar second house of income and what you own, and they meet on July 4. That can look like a surprise expense, a sudden side offer, or a subscription you cancel on principle. Quick money decisions that weekend are easier to live with if they are reversible, and the irreversible ones can wait.

Venus, your ruler, enters Virgo and your fifth house of romance and self-made pleasure on July 9, which sweetens the middle of the month: a date, a studio afternoon, something you make because you want to. July 13 is worth watching, when Venus squares Uranus back in that money house and an impulse purchase may look more convincing than it is. Something inexpensive and enjoyable could be a better plan.

The new moon on July 14 lands in Cancer and your third house of errands, siblings, and the neighborhood. It is a fresh start for a message, a course, or a local commitment. Mercury has been retrograde in that same house all month, though, and it stations direct on July 23. You might draft the email and the agreement now, then send and sign after the 23rd.

The finish is domestic and bright. The Sun enters Leo and your fourth house of home and family on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29. It is a good day for a housewarming, a decision about a place, or a family table with everyone at it. The same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lights your tenth house of career, so something public may peak just as home news arrives. If July 27's opposition between the Sun and Pluto puts a demanding voice from work on the line, it is fine to let it ring. This round can go to the house.

For once the sky moves at your speed. Mars is in Gemini from the first of the month to the last, in your solar first house, and on July 4 it meets Uranus, also in your sign. That is initiative with a live wire in it: the announcement, the haircut, the thing you finally quit. The next day, July 5, Mars trines Pluto and sextiles Neptune, which can give a bold move both traction and a reason. If you have been waiting for a starting signal, this weekend may feel like one.

The money picture asks for more patience. Mercury, your ruler, is retrograde in Cancer, your second house of income, until it stations direct on July 23. The new moon there on July 14 is a good moment to choose a financial goal, such as the rate you will ask for or a budget you can keep. You might set it on the 14th and sign anything after the 23rd. The Sun's square to Saturn on July 6 sketches the tension early, with a cost on one side and a commitment to friends or a long-range plan on the other. If only one gets funded this month, that is fine.
July 19 is quietly useful. Mars in your sign sextiles Saturn in your eleventh house, and the people who share your long game may offer real help. It is worth accepting.

Then the month hands you the microphone. The Sun enters Leo and your third house of messages, pitches, and the near neighborhood on July 22, and meets Jupiter there on July 29, a strong day for talking. It suits sending the pitch, publishing the piece, or making the ask you have been rehearsing. That same day's full moon in Aquarius falls in your ninth house of travel and study. A faraway matter, such as a trip, an application, or an audience in another time zone, may come to a head just as you find the words.

Your year has a natural restart on July 14. The new moon lands at 22° Cancer that morning, in your solar first house, and it is a clean reset. One caveat: Mercury is retrograde in your sign until July 23, so the weeks around the new moon suit revision more than debut. You might rewrite the bio, rebook the appointment, or repair the friendship. A launch may sit better after the 23rd.

July 6 asks for some patience. The Sun in your sign squares Saturn in Aries, your tenth house of career. Think of the deadline that ignores your birthday month, or the boss who wants it anyway. You can meet the obligation without renegotiating your whole job on the spot. Saturn stations retrograde on July 26, and pressure that felt permanent may come up for review through the fall.

Mars spends the month in Gemini, your twelfth house, which is backstage. Its meeting with Uranus on July 4 may register as restlessness with no visible cause, or a sudden wish to vanish for a day. That is less a crisis than a hint about your schedule, and real rest is worth booking. Quiet work counts too. Mars sextiles Saturn on July 19, and something finished in private may earn credit in public.

Then the ledger looks friendlier. The Sun enters Leo and your second house of income on July 22 and meets Jupiter there on July 29, a good money day in your month. It suits sending the invoice, raising the subject of pay, or naming a number without apologizing for it. The same day's full moon in Aquarius falls in your eighth house of shared finances, so a joint matter such as a loan, a reimbursement, or a split may come to a head at the same time. The 29th is a reasonable day to look at it clearly.

The first three weeks are the wind-up. The Sun sits in Cancer, your solar twelfth house of rest and the backstage, until July 22, and Mercury is retrograde there until July 23. The new moon on July 14 lands in that same quiet territory, and it suits closing the old year on purpose. You might cancel what you kept out of politeness, sleep a great deal, and let the drafts stay drafts. Your season is coming, and arriving rested helps.

Your friends may not be resting. Mars and Uranus meet in Gemini, your eleventh house, on July 4. Think of the invitation that appears an hour before the event, or the plan that reroutes twice and improves both times. The holiday weekend may be lively, since that corner of your chart is the loudest one until your own season begins.

Jupiter has been in Leo since June 30, and on July 20 it opposes Pluto in your seventh house of partnership. As your momentum becomes visible, someone close may respond by holding on tighter. The Sun repeats the opposition on July 27. Neither day needs a showdown. It can be enough to say where you are going and to mean the invitation to come along.

Then the sky clears its throat. The Sun enters your sign on July 22 and meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, a bright day in your season. It suits a launch, a party, or the ask that felt too big in March. Because the same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius falls in your partnership house, a relationship may come into clearer focus just as you are most visible. The 29th is a natural point to build toward in July.

Work may get loud before you do. Mars spends July in Gemini, your solar tenth house of career, and it meets Uranus there on July 4. That can look like a reorganization, a scope change, or a client who discovers a deadline over the holiday weekend. If you are the person who can fix it, it helps to say out loud what fixing it costs. July 19, when Mars sextiles Saturn, is a day when things may settle into something durable, such as an approval or a signed-off plan.

Mercury, your ruler, complicates the social calendar. It is retrograde in Cancer, your eleventh house of friends and future plans, until July 23. The new moon there on July 14 can open a new circle or revive an old plan. Confirming every date twice is wise, and the group thread may contradict itself until the 23rd.

Venus enters your sign on July 9, which suits you. For the rest of the month you may look the way you feel on your best days. When Venus squares Uranus on July 13, a chaotic Monday at work could tempt you to reinvent yourself by Friday. A small change, like a haircut, may satisfy that urge better than a large one.

The month ends in a register you like, which is privately. The Sun enters Leo and your twelfth house on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29, a good day that may be invisible to everyone else. It suits a finished draft, a retreat, or a long unscheduled afternoon. That same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in your sixth house of workload and routine, so the sprint you have been running may crest and clear at once. Finishing it and handing it off leaves room for a quiet satisfaction.

The public part of your month comes first. The Sun crosses Cancer, your solar tenth house of career and reputation, until July 22, and the new moon there on July 14 suits a professional reset: an application, a conversation about your title, a portfolio finally reorganized. One timing note: Mercury is retrograde in that same house until July 23, so you might write things on the 14th and submit them after the 23rd.

July 6 names the month's central tension. The Sun squares Saturn in Aries, your seventh house, with the job pulling one way and the partnership the other, and both have a point. Saturn has been asking your closest relationship to mature all year. It stations retrograde on July 26, and the agreements you made in spring may come up for review through the fall. Reading them over together may work better than doing it separately.

Two smaller currents are worth using. Mars and Uranus meet in Gemini, your ninth house, on July 4. If a trip suggests itself out of nowhere, it may be worth a look. Venus, your ruler, slips into Virgo and your twelfth house on July 9, which favors scheduling some real solitude, because the social battery is not infinite.

You may want it charged. The Sun enters Leo and your eleventh house of friends on July 22, then meets Jupiter there on July 29, a good social day and a likely setting for a useful introduction. The same day's full moon at 6° Aquarius lights your fifth house of romance and creative work, so something you love may come into full view in front of people who appreciate it. The 29th could be a good night to go out and stay late.

Distance may suit you this month. The July 14 new moon at 22° Cancer lands in your solar ninth house of travel, study, and what you actually believe. It is a fresh start for a course, a trip you finally plan, or a conviction you say out loud. One asterisk: Mercury is retrograde in the same territory until it stations direct on July 23, so you might sketch the itinerary early and buy the nonrefundable parts after that date. The Sun's square to Saturn on July 6 names the obstacle in advance. Your workload may argue that you cannot possibly leave, though that argument is worth questioning.

Mars spends July in Gemini, your eighth house of shared money and private arrangements, and the opening weekend may be loud. Mars meets Uranus on July 4, which can bring a surprise statement, a jolt to a joint account, or a renegotiation nobody scheduled. The next day is easier than it looks. Mars trines Pluto on July 5, your two rulers cooperating, which favors a deliberate money conversation over a reactive one. If something needs signing, the Mars sextile to Saturn on July 19 is a steady day for it.

Career is the larger story late in the month. Jupiter is newly settled in Leo, your tenth house, and the Sun joins it on July 22, then meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, a good professional day. It could suit something visible such as a pitch, a review, or a launch. Something pulls the other way, though. Jupiter opposes Pluto on July 20, and the Sun repeats it on July 27, both along the axis that reaches your fourth house of home. The July 29 full moon lands at 6° Aquarius in that very house. On a day when work goes well, something domestic may also come to a head, and dinner at home may matter as much as the meeting.

The stations are quieter weather. Neptune turns retrograde on July 7 and Saturn on July 26, both in your sixth house of routines and health. The regimen you built this spring may come up for review through the end of the year. The parts you actually do are the ones worth keeping.

Jupiter, your planet, is settling into Leo and your solar ninth house of travel, study, and the far edge of the map, and July gives it a warm welcome. The Sun arrives in Leo on July 22 and meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, a good day in your month. It could suit a trip, an exam, or publishing something you have been working on. Jupiter's trine to Neptune on July 20 adds imagination to the planning, so the destination that sounds slightly implausible may be worth pricing.

Partnership supplies the plot twists. Mars is in Gemini, your seventh house, all month, and it meets Uranus on July 4. The person closest to you may do something unscripted. Giving it room can help, since the relationship may be asking for movement rather than an exit. Venus enters Virgo and your tenth house of career on July 9, and its square to Uranus on July 13 can put your work schedule and your partner's spontaneity briefly at odds. Mars sextiles Saturn on July 19, which favors a plan made together that holds.

Shared money asks for patience first. The Sun squares Saturn on July 6, an obligation involving someone else's resources pressing on your own commitments. Mercury is retrograde in your eighth house until July 23, so joint paperwork signed before then may come back for edits. The new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer in that same house, suits an honest reset: a shared budget talked through, an application started clean. Signatures may sit better after the 23rd.

One review notice: Saturn stations retrograde on July 26 in your fifth house, where Neptune has been retrograde since July 7. A romantic or creative commitment from the spring may come up for reconsideration through the end of the year. Meanwhile the July 29 full moon at 6° Aquarius fills your third house of messages on the same day as the Jupiter meeting, so the phone may be busy. A sibling might be the first call worth returning.

On July 6 the Sun squares Saturn, your planet, and the month states its theme early. The Sun sits in Cancer, your solar seventh house of partnership. Saturn sits in Aries, your fourth house of home and family. Someone close may want more from you than the household has to spare, or the household may want more than the relationship does. Neither side is wrong, and the week may need setting aside for it.

Some repair is available mid-month. The new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer, is a clean start in that same partnership house. It suits an honest conversation, a second chance, or a contract renewed on better terms. Mercury has been retrograde there all month and stations direct on July 23, so anything negotiated before that date may deserve one more read after it. Old agreements that resurface in early July are material for the new moon, not verdicts.

Work may run hot and then settle. Mars conjunct Uranus on July 4, in your sixth house of routines, can look like a schedule flipped without notice: an outage, a coverage gap, a reorganized week. Mars sextile Saturn on July 19 favors a fix that holds, and it is a sensible day to set a new routine.

Money is the late-month story, on both sides of the ledger. Jupiter opposes Pluto on July 20 across your eighth and second houses, the line between what you share and what is yours. The Sun repeats the question on July 27. On July 29 the Sun meets Jupiter at 6° Leo in your eighth house, a supportive day for a loan, a settlement, or a partner's good news. The full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in your second house the same day, which makes that morning a natural time to send an invoice.

Saturn itself stations retrograde on July 26 in your fourth house. The home project or family arrangement you committed to this spring may come up for review through the end of the year. You might keep the load-bearing parts and renegotiate the rest.

For once, the month's closing act is addressed to you. The July 29 full moon lands at 6° Aquarius, your solar first house, and much of what comes before it reads as buildup. First-house culminations are personal. You may notice something about how you live, look, or introduce yourself coming into fuller view, with other people watching.

The buildup runs through partnership. Jupiter is in Leo, your seventh house, and on July 20 it opposes Pluto in your own sign. That can feel like a partner's growth pressing on who you are becoming: an offer to merge homes, calendars, or plans that is generous and a little engulfing at once. The Sun repeats the opposition on July 27, then meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, a warm day that can belong to the two of you. It is a good day to make the offer or consider accepting it. Under your own full moon that same evening, it may be worth checking that the arrangement still fits the person you actually are.

Romance and side projects get the early sparks. Mars in Gemini, your fifth house, meets Uranus, your planet, on July 4. Think of the spontaneous date, the idea that arrives sideways, or the collaboration that starts as a joke. Mars trines Pluto the next day, July 5, which lends staying power. Whatever sparks that weekend can become serious if you want it to.

The unglamorous middle matters too. The Sun squares Saturn on July 6, with your workload leaning on the errands and paperwork of your third house. The new moon on July 14, at 22° Cancer in your sixth house, suits a reset of routine: the sleep schedule, the checkup, the calendar rebuilt around how you actually work. Mercury is retrograde in that same house until July 23, so appointment times may shift until then. Saturn stations retrograde on July 26 in your third, and a writing project or sibling arrangement may come up for review. That can read as a pause rather than a cancellation.

July 14 is worth circling. The new moon that day, at 22° Cancer, lands in your solar fifth house of romance, play, and the creative work that is yours alone. It is a clean fresh start in your summer, suited to asking someone out, starting the draft, or booking studio time. The footnote is Mercury, retrograde in that same house until July 23. An old flame who resurfaces or a stalled project that stirs in early July may deserve a look, though committing to either can wait until after the 23rd.

Partnership warms up. Venus enters Virgo, your seventh house, on July 9, and much of the month may feel easier for couples and close collaborators. The one dated bump is July 13, when Venus squares Uranus and a household surprise could test everyone's patience. It may be an aftershock of July 4, when Mars met Uranus in your fourth house and something at home changed without asking first: the appliance, the roommate's announcement, the sudden idea about moving. Estimates can be gathered early. Mars sextile Saturn on July 19 is a steadier day for the repair, the quote, or the family decision.

Work can grow pleasantly if you pace it. Jupiter is in Leo, your sixth house of routines and health, and the Sun joins it on July 22, then meets Jupiter at 6° Leo on July 29, a bright day this month. A bigger role may be worth considering then. The caution is the axis it sits on. Jupiter opposed Pluto on July 20, the Sun repeats it on July 27, and both point at your twelfth house of rest. More work tends to hold up only when recovery is scheduled alongside it. Fittingly, the July 29 full moon at 6° Aquarius lands in that twelfth house the same day, so a quiet evening may suit.

About money: the Sun's square to Saturn on July 6 weighs the month's fun against the budget. Saturn stations retrograde in your second house on July 26, with Neptune retrograde there since July 7, and the fall can be a time to review the spending plan. Nothing dramatic needs deciding. You can keep paying the same bills and let the numbers sit still for a while.

August starts by asking what you are willing to take seriously because you enjoy it. Leo is your solar fifth house of pleasure, romance, and self-made work, and the Sun trines Saturn in Aries on August 7. That is less glamour than practice: the date that deserves planning, the creative thing that needs a schedule, the child or project that wants your steadier attention.

The middle of the month is louder there. Mercury enters Leo on August 9 and meets a stack of aspects on Wednesday, August 12: opposition Pluto, trine Neptune, sextile Uranus. That same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. A simple announcement may serve you best, since the audience, the dream, and the surprise variable are all in the room. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, and Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17. If you have a pitch, an invitation, or an opening night in mind, the 15th to the 17th is a friendly stretch to consider.

Partnership gets its own chapter once Venus enters Libra on August 6. The Venus trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 can make a relationship feel both fated and difficult to read. The plain question usually helps. By August 21, when Venus opposes Saturn in your sign, any answer has to live inside time, limits, and actual behavior.

Home asks for care rather than drama. Mars enters Cancer on August 11 and squares Neptune on August 17, which can fog a family conversation or household plan. The righteous speech can wait until you know what happened. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23, Mercury follows on August 25, and the August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lands in your twelfth house. Rest is not a moral failure. That same day, Mercury and the Sun both square Uranus, and the calendar may shift. You can let it.

August begins at home. Leo is your solar fourth house, and on August 7 the Sun trines Saturn from that private territory to your twelfth house of rest. The theme is plain: a quieter house, a real boundary, and less calling exhaustion a personality trait.

The domestic reset arrives on Wednesday, August 12. Mercury, newly in Leo since August 9, opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus that day, and the new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo. A family conversation, lease matter, renovation, or room-by-room decision may move fast. A flexible plan helps, since Uranus is in Gemini, your second house, and any surprise could carry a cost. Mercury meets Jupiter in Leo on August 15, a warmer day for the generous version: the family table, good news, a big yes about where you live.

Venus, your planet, enters Libra on August 6 and your sixth house of work, health, and the small systems that keep a life running. Its trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 asks whether the routine serves your future or just looks graceful from the outside. The Venus-Jupiter sextile on August 17 helps, and the Venus-Saturn opposition on August 21 suggests the help needs structure.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your third house of messages and local motion. When Mars squares Neptune on August 17, a confusing text may be better answered once the anger passes. By August 23 the Sun enters Virgo, your fifth house, and Mercury follows on August 25. Pleasure returns, and the August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lights your eleventh house of friends just as Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. If the group plan changes, the second version may be the better one.

August hands you the microphone and asks you to use it carefully. Leo is your solar third house of messages, siblings, errands, and the near neighborhood. Mercury, your planet, enters Leo on August 9, and by Wednesday, August 12 it is opposite Pluto, trine Neptune, and sextile Uranus in Gemini. A sentence can have reach, and it can also have consequences. The true thing can be said without making it harder than truth requires.

That same day, the new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo. It is a natural start for a writing project, local commitment, conversation, class, or pitch. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15 in the same house, a good day for words that need to travel: the proposal, the announcement, the application, the message you want forwarded.

Money and workload ask for cleaner edges. Venus enters Libra on August 6, your fifth house, and August 10 can feel both magnetic and confusing as Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune. You can enjoy the invitation without turning it into a life plan by midnight. Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your second house, then squares Neptune on August 17. A cost may be blurry, or a desire may be dressed up as necessity. Getting the number in writing helps.

August 17 also brings Mercury trine Saturn and Venus sextile Jupiter, so the day that muddles one corner may steady another. The version with a receipt and a calendar tends to hold. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, moving attention to home and family. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lights your career house while Mercury and the Sun both square Uranus in your sign. A public matter may come to a head, and your private life may not stay quiet while it does.

The month is blunt about money, value, and what you are willing to ask for. Leo is your solar second house, and on August 7 the Sun trines Saturn from there to your career house. A rate, role, invoice, or budget can get real when you treat it as a grown-up matter instead of a hope.

The middle of the month does more. Mercury enters Leo on August 9, then opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus on Wednesday, August 12. That same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. It is a natural point to start a new money plan, with room for the hidden detail: taxes, shared resources, a friend's advice, or the private fear that has been steering the numbers. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, and Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17. If you need to name a number, that window is a friendly one.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, giving you more heat than usual. It is useful if aimed. On August 17 Mars squares Neptune in Aries, your tenth house, and a vague professional pressure could start to feel like a personal emergency. Asking what is actually due, by whom, and when may help. The answer may be smaller than the feeling.

Home softens once Venus enters Libra on August 6. Its trine to Pluto and opposition to Neptune on August 10 can make a family or household matter feel tender and overlarge at once. By August 21, when Venus opposes Saturn, a repair may need a boundary as well as goodwill. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, shifting you into messages and local logistics. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lights your ninth house of travel, study, and belief while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. A route may change, and the larger direction does not have to.

This is your month, but not the loud kind. The Sun is in Leo until August 23, your solar first house, and it trines Saturn on August 7. That supports serious self-definition: the promise you can keep, the plan you can repeat, the version of confidence that does not need applause to stand up.

The main reset arrives on Wednesday, August 12. The new moon, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo. Mercury, newly in your sign since August 9, spends the same day opposite Pluto, trine Neptune, and sextile Uranus. You may hear yourself say something that changes the room. Pluto is in your partnership house, though, and the other person is not a prop in your reveal. Mercury meets Jupiter in Leo on August 15, a good day to consider the announcement, the ask, the introduction, or a first step into a larger role.

Venus enters Libra on August 6, sweetening your third house of messages and local plans. August 10 is more complicated: Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune, so a conversation can feel intimate and slightly unreal at once. It can stay beautiful while you check the facts. Venus sextile Jupiter on August 17 is easier, and Venus opposition Saturn on August 21 asks whether the words match the commitment.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your twelfth house, and squares Neptune on August 17. Restlessness may have no obvious target, and there is no need to invent one. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23, Mercury follows on August 25, and attention turns to money and self-worth. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lights shared resources while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus in your friendship house. Someone's plan could change the math. Recalculating before you react is the calmer path.

The first three weeks are backstage. Leo is your solar twelfth house of rest, privacy, and unfinished business, and the Sun trines Saturn on August 7. That favors useful solitude: the appointment kept, the old obligation closed, the quiet discipline that supports the year ahead.

Mercury, your planet, enters Leo on August 9 and makes August 12 unusually busy behind the curtain: opposition Pluto, trine Neptune, sextile Uranus. The same day brings the new moon, a total solar eclipse, at 20° Leo. Something private may be ready for a reset, such as a sleep pattern, a secret worry, a draft, or a goodbye. There is no need to rush it into public. Mercury meets Jupiter on August 15, still in that hidden house, and any good news may feel more like relief than applause.

Money may go better with good manners once Venus enters Libra on August 6, your second house. Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune on August 10. An opportunity can be real while the shared-cost piece stays foggy, so the extra question is worth asking. Venus sextile Jupiter on August 17 can help you get paid for work done quietly, while Venus opposite Saturn on August 21 asks for a cleaner boundary around debt, obligation, or someone else's expectations.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your eleventh house of friends and future plans, then squares Neptune on August 17. A group promise may be badly defined, and names next to tasks help. Your season begins when the Sun enters Virgo on August 23, and Mercury follows on August 25. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lands in your partnership house while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus in your career house. A relationship may reach clarity just as work changes shape. You can answer both, one at a time.

Your month starts in the room where people know your name. Leo is your solar eleventh house of friends, collaborators, and future plans. The Sun trines Saturn on August 7, and a group plan can become real when someone finally agrees to the structure. That someone could be you if nobody else volunteers.

Venus, your planet, enters Libra on August 6. It brings back some social ease, though not a free pass to blur yourself into everyone else's weather. August 10 is the test: Venus trines Pluto and opposes Neptune, pulling romance, friendship, and partnership into the same charged frame. If a bond feels enormous, it may deserve a little time before you rename your life around it. Venus sextiles Jupiter on August 17, an easier day for pleasure, introductions, and good company. Venus opposes Saturn on August 21, and the same relationship may need to show its practical side.

The new moon on Wednesday, August 12, a total solar eclipse, lands at 20° Leo in your eleventh house. Mercury entered Leo on August 9 and also opposes Pluto, trines Neptune, and sextiles Uranus that day. It suits the start of a shared project, as long as nobody pretends everyone has the same motive. The motive does not need to be pure. It does help if it is spoken.

Mars enters Cancer on August 11, your career house, then squares Neptune on August 17. A public obligation could become strangely slippery: unclear authority, vague instructions, a moving target. Getting it in writing helps. The Sun enters Virgo on August 23 and Mercury follows on August 25, moving you toward rest. The August 28 full moon, a deep partial lunar eclipse at 4.9° Pisces, lights your workload while Mercury and the Sun square Uranus. If the schedule shifts, doing less and doing it better is a reasonable answer.

August is public. Leo is your solar tenth house of career, reputation, and the thing people can point to. The Sun trines Saturn on August 7, and the month favors work with a spine: the portfolio cleaned up, the title clarified, the responsibility named instead of carried invisibly.

The career reset lands on Wednesday, August 12. Mercury has just entered Leo on August 9, and on the 12th it opposes Pluto in your fourth house, trines Neptune in your sixth, and sextiles Uranus in your eighth. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, connecting that partnership house to Jupiter in Leo and your fifth house of pleasure and things you make: an easy yes, offered rather than negotiated. October 16 is the month's most usable day. Mars in Leo trines Saturn at 10.4°, so ambition and patience point the same direction, and Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your eleventh house, unsticking something in a group you belong to.

The last week turns slower. Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, back in that shared-money territory. Expect a contract to be reread, and read it. Venus re-enters Libra on October 25, still retrograde, which returns the partnership question to the table with a softer face. Then October 26 does two things at once: the full moon at 2.8° Taurus lights your second house, where your own money and what you actually value come to a head, and the Sun squares Pluto. Decide what is yours before you decide what to share.

Your ruler turns around this month, and the full moon lands in your own sign. Venus stations retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3, in your solar seventh house of partnership: six weeks of revisiting one relationship rather than starting another. On October 4 the Sun opposes Saturn at 11.3°, the Sun in Libra and your sixth house of work and health against Saturn retrograde in your twelfth. Tiredness is information here. Something in the routine is costing more than it returns.

The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is the reset for exactly that: the schedule, the appointment you keep moving, the habit. It is a small, practical beginning and it holds if you keep it small. Mars spends the month in Leo and your fourth house of home and family (trine Neptune on October 2, opposite Pluto on October 3, sextile Uranus on October 7), so the household is where the energy and the friction both live. On October 16 Mars trines Saturn at 10.4° and that domestic effort finally gets traction, while Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your tenth house and a work situation stalled since spring starts moving again.

On October 23 the Sun enters Scorpio and your partnership house, and the second half of the month belongs to other people. Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, so conversations there will need repeating; say the thing twice and write it down. Venus returns to Libra on October 25, still retrograde, putting the work question back beside the relationship one. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 is yours: something you have been carrying personally reaches its visible end, and the Sun squares Pluto the same day. Let it finish.

Your ruler stations retrograde late in the month, so front-load anything that needs saying cleanly. October opens with Mercury square Pluto on October 2 (a conversation carrying more pressure than its subject deserves) and with Mars in Leo, your solar third house of talk, errands and the near neighbourhood, running three contacts in a week: trine Neptune on October 2, opposite Pluto on October 3, sextile Uranus at 5.4° on October 7. That last one is the good one. Uranus is retrograde in your own sign, and the sextile is the day an idea about yourself arrives usable rather than disruptive.

The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your fifth house of pleasure, romance and the things you make for their own sake. It is the month's genuine beginning, and it wants play rather than output. The Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° on October 15, linking that fifth house to Jupiter in Leo and your third: the pitch, the post, the sentence that carries further than expected. On October 16 Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your ninth house, and a long question about study, belief or somewhere you want to live stops circling.

Then the month narrows. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your sixth house of work and health; Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same house. Expect the schedule to argue with itself for a few weeks. That is not the week to add a commitment. Reread the last one instead. Venus re-enters Libra on October 25 while retrograde, warming the creative house again, and the full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something private in your twelfth. Rest is the correct answer to that one.

Home is the month's centre of gravity. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar fourth house of home, family and where you are from. It is the cleanest reset of your year for the living situation, the room, the family arrangement. Before it, on October 4, the Sun opposes Saturn at 11.3°, that home angle against Saturn retrograde in your tenth house of work and public standing. It is the old argument between what the household needs and what the job takes. This year it is worth answering rather than postponing.

Mars spends October in Leo and your second house of money and what you own, which is unusually useful: trine Neptune on October 2, sextile Uranus on October 7, and trine Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That last day is when earning and patience line up and a practical money move actually works. Mars opposes Pluto on October 3, across to your eighth house of shared and borrowed money, so early in the month one figure will feel like a power question. It is arithmetic. Treat it that way. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius on October 16 in that same eighth house, and something contractual frozen since spring begins to move.

Venus is retrograde from October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio, in your fifth house: an old affection, an old creative project, or a child's situation coming back for another look. It returns to Libra and your home angle on October 25, still retrograde, which draws the two threads together. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and the fifth house warms; Mercury stations retrograde there at 21.0° on October 24. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your eleventh house of friends and groups: one circle reaches its natural end or its clear commitment.

Mars is in your sign for the whole of October, and it does not sit still. It trines Neptune on October 2, opposes Pluto at 3.1° on October 3, sextiles Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. Read that as a sequence: imagination, then a collision with someone else's will in your solar seventh house of partnership, then a fast opening, then, best of the four, the day your drive and your patience finally agree. October 16 is the day to push something heavy uphill.

Jupiter is also in Leo, and on October 15 the Sun sextiles it at 22.0° from Libra and your third house of conversation and short trips. Say the thing. It travels further than you expect that week, and Jupiter in your own sign means the reception is warmer than the message strictly earns. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 resets that third house: a new rhythm of correspondence, a local arrangement, a sibling conversation restarted. The Sun opposed Saturn at 11.3° on October 4 before it, so the first week has the sharper tone: someone slows you down and you dislike it.

The second half moves indoors. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your fourth house of home, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same place, and household logistics will need doing twice. Venus has been retrograde there since October 3, at 8.5° Scorpio, so the home question has been open all month; it moves to your third house on October 25, still retrograde. Then the full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 tops your tenth house of career, and something public completes. Pluto turned direct in your partnership house on October 16, and that is the quieter story underneath.

Money is the visible thread and health is the hidden one. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your solar second house of income, possessions and what you are worth. It is the clearest financial restart of your year, and one worth making a plan around rather than a wish. It follows the Sun's opposition to Saturn at 11.3° on October 4, that money house against Saturn retrograde in your eighth: your resources against a shared obligation, stated plainly by someone else. Attend to the number, not the tone.

Your ruler has a complicated month. Mercury squares Pluto on October 2 and stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, both in your third house of talk, errands and the local round. Between those dates, say the important things. After October 24, repeat them. Venus is retrograde from October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio in that same third house, which doubles the theme: old messages, old routes, an old neighbour or sibling thread reopening. Venus returns to Libra and your money house on October 25, still retrograde, so a price you agreed earlier comes back for review.

Two days carry the month's better weather. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, connecting your income to Jupiter in Leo and your twelfth house: help arrives from somewhere unadvertised, and you should accept it. On October 16 Mars in Leo trines Saturn at 10.4° while Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your sixth house of work and health: a body or work-shaped problem immovable since spring starts to shift, and you have the stamina that day to act on it. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your ninth house: a course, a trip, a conviction reaching its end.

This is your season and it is not a simple one. The Sun is in your sign until October 23, and the new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is your solar first house reset, the annual beginning that sets the tone for how you present yourself and what you start. Make it concrete. Before it, on October 4, the Sun opposes Saturn at 11.3° from your seventh house: a partner or close counterpart names a constraint, and October's work is deciding how much of it you accept.

Your ruler turns retrograde early. Venus stations at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3, in your second house of money and self-worth, and re-enters your own sign on October 25 still moving backwards. Read the whole month as a re-pricing: what you charge, what you accept, what you thought you were worth in August. The answer arrives slowly and should not be forced. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, linking your first house to Jupiter in Leo and your eleventh: friends and networks are the easy route this month, and one introduction is worth more than a fortnight of effort.

October 16 unsticks things. Mars trines Saturn at 10.4° and Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your fifth house, where a creative project or a romance frozen since spring starts to move again. Then the tone changes: the Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your money house, Mercury stations retrograde there at 21.0° on October 24, and financial admin gets slower and more careful. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your eighth house of shared resources, and the Sun squares Pluto the same day. Something jointly held reaches its decision point. You will have the information by then.

Almost everything happens in your sign this month, and most of it moves backwards. Venus stations retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3, in your solar first house: six weeks of reconsidering how you look, what you want and who you want it from. Mercury squared Pluto from your sign on October 2 and stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24. The Sun arrives on October 23. So the last ten days put the Sun, a retrograde Mercury and your birthday season in the same place: loud, personal, and not the week for a final decision.

The first three weeks are quieter than that sounds. The Sun spends them in Libra and your twelfth house, which is the year's rest window whether or not you take it. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is a private beginning: something started alone, unannounced, and better for it. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in your tenth house of career: a good word said about you in a room you are not in. On October 16 Mars in Leo trines Saturn at 10.4° and Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius in your fourth house of home and family, where a long-stuck domestic matter finally gives.

Two things then land together on October 26. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus culminates in your seventh house (a partnership reaches its visible peak or its honest end) and the Sun squares Pluto from your sign to that home angle. Between Venus retrograde in your first house and Mercury retrograde behind it, the instruction for the last week is narrow: gather the facts, say less than you want to, and let November decide. Venus leaves for Libra on October 25, which takes some of the heat out of it.

Your people are the month's best resource. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar eleventh house of friends, groups and shared projects. It is the cleanest reset of your year for who you spend time with and what you are building together. Ask for the introduction in the fortnight after it. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0°, and your ruler is in Leo and your ninth house of travel, study and conviction: the connection that opens a door somewhere further away than your current map.

Mars is in that ninth house all month and it is the engine. It trines Neptune on October 2, opposes Pluto on October 3 (a plan meets a flat refusal from your third house of everyday communication), sextiles Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That last day is when the far plan becomes a booked, paid, scheduled thing rather than an intention. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your third house, and a conversation frozen since spring restarts.

The end of the month asks for quiet, which you will resist. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your twelfth house; Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24 in the same place. Old thoughts come back around, and most of them want reviewing rather than acting on. Venus has been retrograde there since October 3 at 8.5° Scorpio, so something unfinished and private has already been asking for attention. It moves to your eleventh house on October 25, still retrograde. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your sixth house of work and health: a routine reaches the point where it either changes or stays for good.

Your career angle carries the Sun for three weeks and the year's clearest professional reset. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 opens your solar tenth house: a new role, a new title, or the same job restated on different terms. Start it deliberately. On October 4 the Sun opposed Saturn at 11.3°, your ruler retrograde in your fourth house of home, so the month's underlying tension is the honest one: what the work demands against what the household is owed. Saturn retrograde means the answer is a renegotiation, not a resignation.

Mars spends October in Leo and your eighth house of shared money, debt and other people's resources. It opposes Pluto on October 3 (one financial arrangement shows its teeth) and trines Saturn at 10.4° on October 16, which is the day to restructure rather than argue. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your second house of income, and money stuck since spring begins to move. Mid-month is where your leverage is: on October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in that eighth house, and someone with resources says yes.

Venus stationed retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3 in your eleventh house of friends and networks, so a professional friendship is under quiet review all month; it returns to your career house on October 25, still retrograde, which brings the review to the surface. The Sun enters Scorpio on October 23, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, and group logistics get slower. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates in your fifth house of pleasure and the things you make: a personal project reaches its finish, with the Sun square Pluto the same day. Take the finish.

Pluto is in your sign and October keeps knocking on it. Mercury squares Pluto at 3.1° on October 2, Mars opposes it on October 3, Venus squares it on October 20 and the Sun squares it on October 26: four contacts to the same degree of your solar first house in one month. The theme is consistent: other people press on who you are becoming, and the pressure is not personal even when it feels it. Between them, on October 16, Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius. That is the month's real event, and something in your own long remaking stops circling.

Mars is in Leo and your seventh house for the whole month, which is where the friction arrives from. The opposition on October 3 is the sharpest day; the sextile to Uranus at 5.4° on October 7 and the trine to Saturn at 10.4° on October 16 are the workable ones, when a partner's drive and yours point the same way. Jupiter is in that house too, and the Sun sextiles it at 22.0° on October 15 from your ninth house of travel and study: a partnership that opens a bigger horizon rather than closing one.

The Sun spends three weeks in Libra and that ninth house, and the new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 is the reset for it: the course, the trip, the argument you have decided to take seriously. Then the Sun enters Scorpio on October 23 and your tenth house of career, Mercury stations retrograde at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24, and public matters need double-checking for a few weeks. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 culminates at home, in your fourth house. Something about where you live reaches its answer.

October's money is other people's. The new moon at 17.4° Libra on October 10 falls in your solar eighth house of shared accounts, debts and what is inherited: a genuine restart for a joint arrangement, and the best fortnight of the year to renegotiate one. It follows the Sun's opposition to Saturn at 11.3° on October 4, that eighth house against Saturn retrograde in your second: someone else's terms against your own resources, said out loud. Neither side is unreasonable. Write the numbers down.

Venus stations retrograde at 8.5° Scorpio on October 3 in your ninth house of travel, study and belief, and Mercury stations retrograde there too, at 21.0° Scorpio on October 24. A plan to go somewhere, learn something or commit to a view gets reviewed twice over. That is not an obstruction; it is a chance to find the flaw while it is still cheap. The Sun enters Scorpio and that house on October 23, so the last week has the appetite even while the rest counsels patience.

Mars spends the month in Leo and your sixth house of work and health: opposite Pluto on October 3, sextile Uranus at 5.4° on October 7, trine Saturn at 10.4° on October 16. That trine is the month's most productive day for anything needing sustained effort. Pluto stations direct at 3.1° Aquarius the same day in your twelfth house, and something carried privately since spring starts to lift. On October 15 the Sun sextiles Jupiter at 22.0° in your sixth: a practical offer of help at work. The full moon at 2.8° Taurus on October 26 completes something in your third house: a conversation, a piece of writing, a local matter finishes.

Two reversals end a day apart this month, and most of November arranges itself around them. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar eighth house of shared money and terms agreed to in a hurry. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the partnership house next door. Two adjacent rooms, both under review, both let go.

The approach is gentler than the arrival. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, Libra to Leo, your seventh house in easy contact with your fifth, where pleasure and the things you make live. Then the new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 restarts the shared account four days before Mercury turns. The reset lands before the planet of terms moves, so this is the fortnight the joint money question gets loud rather than settled.

November 16 is the loud one. Mars, your ruler, meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo, both in your fifth house: appetite and scale at the same degree, pointed at whatever you do for the pleasure of doing it. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1°, Scorpio against Leo, the eighth house asking the fifth what all this costs. Hear the question out before you answer it.

Then the month opens outward. The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and your ninth house of distance and study, and trines Neptune in your own sign at 1.7° on November 24, the same day the full moon at 2.3° Gemini fills your third house with every local, half written thing. November 25 is crowded: Sun sextile Pluto at 3.5°, Sun opposite Uranus at 3.7°, and Mars into Virgo and your sixth house, where the Leo blaze becomes a list. On November 30 the Sun trines Saturn at 8.0°, Saturn still in Aries. The question it has put to you all year, what you can actually sustain, gets asked gently for once.

Your ruling planet spends the first half of November still moving backwards. Venus stations direct on November 14 at 22.9° Libra, in your solar sixth house of work, health and the ordinary shape of a week, so the first fortnight is an approach, not a start. Venus sextiles Jupiter on November 4 at 24.7°, tying that work house to Jupiter in Leo and your fourth house of home: an easing between the job and the household.

The new moon on November 9 at 16.9° Scorpio lands in your seventh house, the one part of the chart that is not about you. Four days later Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in the same house. Two retrogrades ending within a day of each other, one in the house of the other person and one in the house of your working week: that pairing is the month. This is the fortnight the stalled conversation gets its words back.

November 16 is loud at home. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your fourth house, and on November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio, so the household and the partnership pull against each other in one week. The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and your eighth house of shared money and debts.

Then both ends of the money question light up. The full moon on November 24 at 2.3° Gemini falls in your second house, your own earnings and what you actually value, and on November 25 the Sun opposes Uranus across that same axis at 3.7°. Mars enters Virgo the same day, which gives your hands somewhere easier to go. On November 29 Uranus trines Pluto at 3.5°, a slow agreement between what you earn and where you stand, and the Sun trines Saturn on November 30. The month ends steadier than it behaved.

The hinge of this month is two days wide and sits right in the middle. Before it, the month is mostly setup. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, linking Venus in Libra, your solar fifth house of pleasure and the things you make, to Jupiter in Leo and your third, where you talk, write and run errands. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 opens the sixth: work, health, the shape of an ordinary day. It is a clean reset, arriving while the traffic is still stopped.

Then the hinge arrives. Mercury, your ruler, stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in that same sixth house, and the rereading ends. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra the next day, November 14. Two retrogrades finishing on consecutive days is the month's real story: both planets stand still before they turn, and the handbrake comes off the work question and the creative one at once. The question they make loud is whether the revising is finished or has become the work.

Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in the third house, Mercury's own territory and so familiar ground. That conjunction is loud wherever it falls, and here it falls on talk. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1°, sixth house against third: the friction between how much you are saying and how much of the day is already spoken for.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your seventh house of partnership on November 22, but the last week is mostly about you. The full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 is in your own sign, with the Sun trine Neptune the same day: something about how you come across reaching its visible end, gently. On November 25 the Sun in Sagittarius opposes Uranus at 3.7° Gemini and asks it again, less gently, while Mars enters Virgo and your fourth house of home. Uranus trines Pluto on November 29. Whatever surfaced, let it stay up.

Two retrogrades end within a day of each other this month, and for you they end in the two rooms that matter most. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar fifth house of romance, play and the things you make. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in your fourth house of home and family. Everything before those two dates is the run-up.

The run-up is warm. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4, linking that home ground to Jupiter in Leo and your second house of earnings and what you value: the household and the money for it in easy contact. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 falls in the fifth house four days ahead of Mercury's turn in the same sign, which gives that creative start a second pass built into the timing. Begin anyway.

November 16 is the loud one. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your second house, appetite and opportunity in the same degree, and this is the week the money question gets loud. Two days later the Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1° on November 18, the fifth house against the second: what you are making, costed against what you are willing to spend on it. Say the number before the enthusiasm does.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your sixth house of work, health and routine on November 22, and two days later the full moon at 2.3° Gemini lands in your twelfth, the unaccounted one. November 24 is a rest reckoning arriving exactly as the schedule tightens. Mars enters Virgo on November 25 and your third house of errands and plain speech sharpens. Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28, closing the loop it opened on November 4, and the Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30, the sixth house meeting the tenth. Nothing in November asks you to settle the whole thing. It asks what you are willing to keep making once the retrogrades stop handing you a reason to wait.

The large fact in your sky is Jupiter in Leo, which is your solar first house: your face, your appetite, the room you take up. Venus sextiles it from Libra on November 4 at 24.7°, out of the third house of talking and writing: a day when phrasing matters more than usual. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 is another register, fourth house, home and foundations, a beginning you make from underneath.

Then two planets turn around on consecutive days. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in that same domestic ground, and Venus does the same at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the house of how you say things. Both had been retrograde: the rereading and the restating that goes with that stops, which is the month's largest event and its quietest. On November 16 Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo, both in the first house, a concentrated shot of personal fuel about as subtle as it sounds. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio, home pulling against the version of you that just caught fire.

The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and the fifth house, familiar ground for a Leo: play, making things, performing because you like to. It trines Neptune at 1.7° on November 24 and the edges soften; the full moon that same day at 2.3° Gemini fills the eleventh house of friends. On November 25 the Sun opposes Uranus at 3.7°, setting what you make alone opposite the crowd it belongs to, and sextiles Pluto at 3.5° Aquarius, which puts a partner in the frame. Mars leaves your sign for Virgo the same day and the heat relocates to earning.

Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28 at 26.7°, the November 4 conversation without the retrograde, and Uranus trines Pluto at 3.5° on November 29. The Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30, fifth house to ninth: what you made for pleasure, set against what you actually believe. Worth asking what the fuel was for.

Two planets turn around a day apart this month, and the first is yours. Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, in your solar third house of talk, messages and the ordinary traffic of the mind. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 sits in the same house four days earlier, which puts a beginning and a reversal in one small room. Whatever you start writing or asking that first week is worth a second pass once your ruling planet turns.

Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra on November 14, in the house of your earnings and what you actually value. Two retrogrades ending that close together is the month's real shape: the sentence you have been trying to word and the number you have been avoiding come up in the same two days. Venus makes an easy angle to Jupiter on November 4 at 24.7° and repeats it on November 28 at 26.7°, Jupiter sitting in Leo and the private twelfth house behind your chart. Neither day asks loudly.

The middle of the month is loud where you cannot watch it. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in that twelfth house: a lot of fuel burning in rest, old business, and the part of your life with no audience. The Sun squares Jupiter at 26.1° on November 18, your third house against that hidden one, and what you want to say rubs against what you are not ready to say.

The Sun enters Sagittarius and your home ground on November 22, and the full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 lights your tenth house of work and public standing while the Sun sits at the base of the chart: house and career at opposite ends of one night. The Sun opposes Uranus at 3.7° on November 25, a degree and a half past where that moon stood. Mars enters Virgo the same day, out of the hidden house and into your own first. The Sun trines Saturn at 8.0° on November 30: a quiet, load-bearing end to a loud month.

Your ruler stops and turns around on November 14. Venus stations direct at 22.9° Libra, in your own sign and your solar first house: the body, the face, the version of you other people meet before you have said anything. Weeks of that running in reverse end here. Ten days earlier, on November 4, retrograde Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7°, Jupiter in Leo and your eleventh house of friends and the long future, which is the easiest room on the chart that week.

The money half runs alongside it. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 lands in your second house, where your earnings and what you count as worth having are kept, and a day before Venus turns, on November 13, Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio in that same house. Two retrogrades ending within a day of each other is November's real story: the number and the self-image come out of review together.

Then it gets loud. Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo on November 16, both in the eleventh, about as much collective heat as a year offers. On November 18 the Sun squares Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio and the second house and the eleventh pull against each other. This is the week what the group wants and what you can afford stop agreeing. The figure is worth saying out loud.

The Sun enters Sagittarius on November 22 and the month moves into your third house: talk, short trips, the people within a mile of you. The full moon at 2.3° Gemini on November 24 lights the ninth house opposite, and the Sun opposes Uranus there on November 25, so the near and the far argue. Mars enters Virgo and your twelfth the same day, where effort goes quiet. Venus sextiles Jupiter again on November 28, at 26.7° and moving forward now, the aspect the month opened with run the right way round. A good month to finish a sentence you started in October.

Two retrogrades end within a day of each other this month, Mercury on November 13 and Venus on November 14, and the first of them ends in your sign. Venus sextiles Jupiter at 24.7° on November 4 ahead of that, still retrograde in Libra and your solar twelfth house of rest and private matters. The new moon at 16.9° Scorpio on November 9 then lands in your first house, the one new moon all year that is simply about you.

Mercury stations direct at 5.0° Scorpio on November 13, after three weeks of walking backwards through it. Venus follows at 22.9° Libra on November 14, so that retrograde ends out of sight, in the twelfth, after beginning in your own sign in early October. Most of the reconsidering happened in plain view. November 16 is the loud one: Mars meets Jupiter at 25.9° Leo in your tenth house of career. The Sun squares that Jupiter from 26.1° Scorpio on November 18, the week the gap between what you want and what the work wants is easiest to measure.
